items.headline: Only about 10% of the S$300m SG Culture Pass was used in its first year
items.summary: In a Sep 2 update, MCCY said just S$30.4 million (about 10%) of the S$300 million fund had been spent by roughly 411,000 Singaporeans as of Aug 31, and that most registered users had not attended a local arts event in five years.

items.headline: Man, 68, dies in a Lorong Lew Lian flat fire as about 30 residents are evacuated
items.summary: A 68-year-old man who lived alone died after a fire broke out in his third-floor Upper Serangoon flat around 2.45pm on Sep 1, with about 30 residents evacuated and three others hospitalised. SCDF is investigating.

items.headline: A nationwide mediation framework for neighbour disputes takes effect from Sep 1
items.summary: From Sep 1 an expanded Mediation Direction framework covers the whole island, authorising HDB and the People's Association to issue Mediation Directions so residents can be steered into mediation earlier in a dispute.

items.headline: Hazy conditions may return to Singapore for up to two weeks amid a regional dry spell
items.summary: MSS warned hazy conditions could occur over the next fortnight as dry weather persists and smoke haze lingers over parts of Sumatra and Kalimantan. The 24-hour PSI was still 'moderate' at 5pm on Sep 1, with highs of 33-35C forecast.

items.headline: India's booming economy and its slumping stock market are increasingly at odds
items.summary: After GDP grew a faster-than-expected 7.8% in the June quarter (manufacturing +9.2%, financial services +12.1%), PM Modi hailed the figures and urged Indians to buy local. Yet the Nifty 50 is down about 8% for the year, among the worst major benchmarks in 2026.

items.headline: Update: The rupee strengthens as RBI measures draw a record US$136 billion in inflows
items.summary: The rupee opened about 69 paise stronger at 94.29 to the dollar on Sep 3, its firmest since late June, after the RBI said special swap and deposit measures had drawn a record US$136 billion in inflows, bolstering its firepower to defend the currency.

items.headline: India and China agree on eight steps to ease border tensions before Xi's Delhi visit
items.summary: Ahead of an expected visit by President Xi Jinping to New Delhi, India and China agreed on eight measures to de-escalate along their disputed Himalayan border. Bilateral trade rose to about US$151.1 billion in the year to March despite years of investment curbs.

items.headline: India's return to active SCO diplomacy signals a careful recalibration under Modi
items.summary: India's fuller engagement at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit reflects a deliberate balancing act, keeping channels open with Beijing and Moscow while guarding its interests. Modi stressed connectivity projects must respect all countries' sovereignty and territorial integrity.

items.headline: UK coverage is unavailable in today's edition
items.summary: The BBC and Sky News (this section's primary outlets) were unreachable from the routine's network today, and no allowed fallback outlet (The Guardian, CNN, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg) surfaced a verifiable UK-domestic story within the run's search budget. The section is held rather than cite an off-list or unverified item.

items.headline: Iran strikes US bases across the Gulf after American attacks on Iran kill 11
items.summary: In the heaviest exchange in over a month, Iran launched drones and missiles at US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan and Iraq on Sep 2, after US strikes on southern Iran killed 11, including five at a wedding in Sirik county. Kuwait and Bahrain said air defences intercepted the fire.

items.headline: Xi Jinping makes his first visit to Egypt in a decade, courting the Middle East
items.summary: President Xi Jinping met President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi in Cairo on Sep 2, his first Egypt visit in 10 years, urging Middle Eastern nations to be 'masters of their own affairs' and pledging to help safeguard regional shipping disrupted by the US-Iran war.

items.headline: Zelensky warns airlines Russian airspace is closing as Putin alleges state terrorism
items.summary: After ordering up to 1,000 long-range drone strikes a day, President Zelensky told carriers on Sep 1 that Russian skies were 'completely unsafe' and notified the ICAO, as flights were cancelled at Moscow's Vnukovo. Putin, speaking in Kyrgyzstan, accused Ukraine of 'state terrorism'.

items.headline: Maduro asks a US judge to dismiss drug charges, citing head-of-state immunity
items.summary: Ousted Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro, 63, and wife Cilia Flores, 69, held in a Brooklyn jail since their Jan 3 capture, filed motions in Manhattan federal court on Sep 3 arguing sovereign immunity bars prosecution. Judge Hellerstein set oral arguments for Nov 17; trial is set for June 1, 2027.

items.headline: Tens of thousands rally across Spain over the Ceuta migrant crisis
items.summary: Protesters filled streets nationwide on Sep 2, roughly 50,000 in Madrid, blaming PM Pedro Sanchez for the crisis after a July surge pushed tens of thousands from Morocco into the enclave of Ceuta, where thousands remain. The rallies coincided with Ceuta Day.

items.headline: Nvidia agrees to buy the AI platform Hugging Face for about US$12.93 billion
items.summary: Nvidia signed a definitive agreement to acquire Hugging Face, the widely used open-source hub for AI models and datasets, for roughly US$12.93 billion, saying it would keep the platform open. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027.

items.headline: AI coding startup Cognition seeks about US$1 billion at a US$47 billion valuation
items.summary: Cognition, maker of the Devin engineering agent, is set to raise around US$1 billion at roughly a US$47 billion valuation, nearly double its US$26 billion mark from May, after annualised revenue passed US$900 million and the round drew close to US$10 billion of interest.

items.headline: OpenAI says its coming 'Astra' model crosses a 'Critical' cyber-risk threshold
items.summary: OpenAI said Astra is the first of its models to reach the 'Critical' cybersecurity tier under its Preparedness Framework, and that it will restrict the model's most advanced offensive-security capabilities to a vetted coalition at launch.

items.headline: Waymo goes on the offensive against Tesla's camera-only approach before Cybercab
items.summary: A week before Tesla's Cybercab event, Waymo argued that 'pure end-to-end' camera-only systems are not yet safe enough, a thinly veiled dig at Tesla, while announcing three new markets. Waymo says it now runs about 4,000 robotaxis across 14 US cities and 500,000 paid trips a week.

items.headline: AI-security firm HiddenLayer raises a US$100 million Series B
items.summary: HiddenLayer, which sells tools to defend machine-learning models from attack, raised a US$100 million Series B led by Delta-v Capital, with participation from Ten Eleven Ventures, Morgan Stanley, Microsoft's M12 and Booz Allen Hamilton.

items.headline: US private payrolls rose just 38,000 in August, the weakest hiring since January
items.summary: ADP reported on Sep 2 that private employers added only 38,000 jobs in August, below the roughly 48,000 consensus and the softest since January. Education and health services added 45,000 while manufacturing shed 17,000, ahead of Friday's official payrolls report.

items.headline: The S&P 500 climbs 1.06% to 7,747.71 as Treasury yields ease
items.summary: US stocks rallied on Sep 3: the S&P 500 rose 1.06% to 7,747.71, the Nasdaq gained 1.4% to 26,584.06 and the Dow added 624 points (1.18%) to 53,686.11, as long-dated Treasury yields retreated and traders trimmed bets on a September Fed rate hike.

items.headline: Brent crude tops US$96 a barrel after Iran fires missiles at Kuwait
items.summary: Oil prices jumped on Sep 3, with Brent trading above US$96 a barrel, after Iran fired drones and missiles at US bases in the Gulf, reigniting fears over supplies through the Strait of Hormuz. OPEC+ core members meet on Sep 6.

items.headline: Broadcom posts record US$29.6 billion in revenue on AI chips, but the shares slip
items.summary: Broadcom reported record fiscal third-quarter revenue of US$29.6 billion, up 86% year on year, with AI semiconductor revenue up 221% to US$16.7 billion, and guided to US$34.8 billion this quarter. Despite the beat and deals with Google, OpenAI and Anthropic, the stock fell next session.

items.headline: F1 Ferrari unveils a Schumacher tribute livery as Monza race week begins
items.summary: With the Italian Grand Prix set for Sep 6, Ferrari revealed a Monza livery marking 30 years since Michael Schumacher signed in 1996. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli, 59 points clear, faces a grid penalty for an engine change, while Lando Norris arrives on a two-win streak about 82 points back.

items.headline: Tennis Sabalenka races past Iatcenko in 53 minutes as Pegula and Navarro advance
items.summary: Top seed and two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka beat Polina Iatcenko 6-1, 6-1 in 53 minutes for her 16th straight US Open win. No. 3 Jessica Pegula downed Sofia Kenin 6-3, 6-1 and Emma Navarro rallied past Caty McNally 3-6, 6-2, 6-3.

items.headline: Tennis Alcaraz recovers to beat Faria as Tiafoe and Medvedev also advance
items.summary: No. 2 seed Carlos Alcaraz dropped the opening set before beating Jaime Faria 4-6, 6-0, 6-3, 6-2 in the US Open second round. Frances Tiafoe beat Rei Sakamoto 6-3, 7-6(2), 7-5 and Daniil Medvedev beat Sebastian Gorzny 6-1, 6-3, 7-5.

items.headline: Cricket Sri Lanka thrash Indonesia by 75 runs at the Women's Asia Cup
items.summary: Defending champions Sri Lanka posted 124 for 7 and bowled Indonesia out for 49 in 18.3 overs for a 75-run win in their Group B match in Dubai, keeping their T20 Asia Cup title defence on track.

items.headline: Cricket Pakistan beat Thailand by 35 runs, setting up a Sep 5 clash with India
items.summary: Pakistan made 119 for 9 and restricted Thailand to 84 for 8 for a 35-run win in their Women's Asia Cup group match in Dubai, building toward the marquee India-Pakistan fixture scheduled for Sep 5.

items.headline: A personalized mRNA vaccine slows melanoma's return in a phase 3 trial
items.summary: In a randomised phase 3 trial of more than 1,000 surgically treated melanoma patients, Merck and Moderna's personalized neoantigen vaccine intismeran, added to Keytruda, significantly slowed recurrence and spread, reported as the first phase 3 success for a personalized cancer vaccine.

items.headline: Mars's southern mantle is found to run 200-400C hotter than the north
items.summary: Applying tidal tomography to decades of orbiter gravity data, a Caltech-led team reports the mantle beneath Mars's southern highlands is 200-400C warmer than the north and partly molten, a possible driver of the planet's crustal dichotomy and magnetic asymmetry.

items.headline: Hubble pins down the earliest known merger in the Milky Way's history
items.summary: Studying 39 globular clusters in the inner galaxy, astronomers found evidence that a dwarf galaxy merged with the young Milky Way about 11.8 billion years ago, pushing back the galaxy's known merger history by roughly 1.8 billion years.

items.headline: Global sea-surface temperature hits a record 21.10C, oddly timed in August
items.summary: EU Copernicus data show the average global sea-surface temperature reached a record 21.10C on Aug 22, edging past the prior high of 21.09C set in March 2024. The August timing is unusual, pointing to an intensifying warm phase.

fun_fact.headline: The first computer bug was a real moth
fun_fact.body: The word 'bug' was already old engineering slang when, on 9 September 1947, operators of Harvard's Mark II found the culprit was a literal one: a moth in Relay 70, taped into the logbook with the note 'First actual case of bug being found'. That page, moth attached, is now in the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History.
fun_fact.source: Smithsonian National Museum of American History; Computer History Museum

puzzle.title: The King's Cellar
puzzle.body: A king has 1,000 bottles of wine and a spy has poisoned exactly one. The poison kills within 24 hours with no earlier symptoms. The feast is in 24 hours. What is the smallest number of prisoner-tasters needed to be certain of identifying the poisoned bottle, and how?
puzzle.approach: Think in binary - a single taster can carry more than one bit of information.
puzzle.answer: 10 prisoners. Number the bottles 0-999 in 10-digit binary (2^10=1024>1000); assign each prisoner one binary place and have them sip from every bottle with a 1 in that place. After 24 hours, the pattern of who died spells the poisoned bottle's number in binary.

word_puzzle.title: Clear a Path
word_puzzle.body: Letter Boxed. Sides - TOP: B I T; RIGHT: R N H; BOTTOM: A S E; LEFT: O M C. Build words of 3+ letters hopping between different sides; each word starts with the previous word's last letter; use all 12 letters. Solve in two words.
word_puzzle.approach: Two words: each word's last letter starts the next, together using all twelve letters, with no same-side hops.
word_puzzle.answer: BRAINSTORM -> MACHETE. BRAINSTORM (B-R-A-I-N-S-T-O-R-M) then MACHETE (starting on the shared M) adds C, H and E, covering all twelve letters with every hop landing on a different side.
